messages:
anya: FYI customer ACME reporting a surge of 502s hitting hosted API since ~15:12 UTC. They see ~30% error rate for text-generation calls. sample trace id: trace-7f9c2a.
anya: attaching minimal repro (curl) and headers we received.
anya: ```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"hello"}' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'```
drew: thanks. do we have any matching ingests in edge logs? can someone pull the frontdoor traces for trace-7f9c2a?
eng-sre-bot: ALERT bridge-edge: increased 502s from eu-hosted-frontdoor cluster over last 6m (p95 latency up from 120ms -> 480ms).
jordan: I briefly scanned the edge dashboard — a handful of upstream auth-cache timeouts correlated with very high Redis latency around 15:10-15:16 UTC. redis-01 showed 600ms p95. that can cause Envoy upstream health failures and 502s.
drew: interesting — did anything deploy right before 15:10? config/infra?
anya: customer says they started a heavy batch of embedding requests but we also rolled out deploy #456 (auth cache change) at 15:05.
jordan: that fits. auth cache change made more calls to Redis on miss, and a tenant burst could cause a cascading latency spike that trips the edge's upstream circuit.
drew: can we repro internally by firing a batch of small requests with auth header churn? steps to repro please.
anya: repro I used: 1) start 200 concurrent POSTs to /v1/generate with unique bearer tokens 2) observe p50/p95 to frontdoor and redis. simple k6 script used.
drew: ok thanks. mitigation? rollback or fallback routing?
jordan: immediate: increase auth-cache local TTL and enable stale-while-revalidate to reduce redis pressure (roll back #456). also bump upstream circuit threshold temporarily. long term: add backpressure on auth refreshes and client-side retry guidance.
support-ops: customer wants a workaround now — can we return a client-side recommendation? e.g., reduce concurrency, add jitter, or set X-Client-Retry: 2 to allow safe retries.
anya: provided customer with temporary guidance and asked if they can throttle to 50 concurrent for next hour while we stabilize.
drew: I'll coordinate a rollback of #456 to canary (eu) and monitor. tagging eng-oncall.
jordan: if rollback not possible quickly, route affected tenant to fallback auth path that reads local token-cache. I'll prep the route rule.
drew: rolled back deploy #456 in eu at 15:28 UTC. observing drop in 502s to normal within ~90s. p95 back to ~130ms.
anya: customer confirmed error rate dropped to ~1% after rollback and they can resume. :relieved:
support-ops: capturing triage notes and will open follow-up ticket for infra team to add redis autoscaling and tighter deploy gating.
anya: filing ticket with steps, logs, and k6 repro. thanks all.
